Language & Runtime Specification

MWM Pseudocode & Interpreter Rules

Bridging the strict typing of Directed Equations with the constructive, step-by-step operational execution of discrete tree machines.

⚖️ 1. The Architectural Duality: Strict Signature vs. Dynamic Execution

In Middle Way Mathematics, every computational algorithm possesses a dual identity. It is simultaneously an axiomatic, machine-certified mathematical identity and an executable, interactive stepper:

The Outer Mathematical Layer Strictly Typed
The Directed Equation (DE):
A formal statement asserting that for all typed inputs on a discrete domain, there exists a unique target in the codomain:
∀ (x₁, x₂) ∈ Domain₁ × Domain₂, ∃! y ∈ Codomain [ y ≔ Rule(x₁, x₂) ]
Anchored directly to Lean 4 / Mathlib formal proofs and domain boundary invariants.
The Inner Operational Layer Dynamic Stepper
The Pseudocode Interpreter:
The constructive witness demonstrating how the result y is obtained in finite mechanical steps:
rule Cut(L: Node, R: Node) : Node ≔ ... begin while ... return candidate; end;
Operates as a generator-driven state machine recording machine telemetry (call depth, step count, tree cuts, additions).
💡 The Mathematical Opportunity of this Asymmetry

Why is the outer boundary strictly typed while the internal body is dynamically interpreted?

  • Zero Educational Friction: Students and authors do not have to fight rigid type-inference compilers for simple loops, index slices, and set aggregations.
  • Strict Boundary Invariants: The outer signature guarantees that inputs and outputs obey domain contracts (such as Conway Node paths {+, -}*, dyadic rationals 𝔻, or hyperreals ℝ_ω), preventing invalid state transitions between curriculum levels.
  • Constructive Witness: Every Directed Equation is not merely an abstract equality; it is grounded by an operational pseudocode algorithm that computes the value on the discrete tree.

📜 2. Lexical Grammar & Concrete Syntax

MWM Pseudocode uses a clean, Pascal-inspired structured syntax featuring explicit rule headers, local variable declarations, and begin ... end; statement blocks.

Rule Declaration Structure

rule RuleName(param1: Domain1, param2: Domain2) : Codomain ≔
var
    localVar1, localVar2: DomainType;
    counter: Integer;
begin
    // 1. Algorithmic assignments
    localVar1 := EmptySet();

    // 2. Structured control flow
    for counter := 0 to 10 do
    begin
        if condition then
            localVar1 := localVar1 ++ '+'
        else
            localVar1 := localVar1 ++ '-';
    end;

    // 3. Constructive Return
    return localVar1;
end;

Reserved Keywords

Category Keywords Operational Semantics
Declaration rule, function, var Defines the algorithm signature, input slots, and local variable scope frame.
Block Delimiters begin, end, return Encloses execution bodies; return halts execution and emits the output.
Conditionals if, then, else Binary branching based on Boolean truth (truth values in 𝔹 = {true, false}).
Counted Loops for, to, do Deterministic iteration over discrete natural intervals [start .. end] ⊂ ℕ.
Collection Loops for each, in, do Iterates through items in a finite tree set (e.g. for each xL in XL do).
While Loops while, do Guarded iteration (e.g. stepping down tree nodes until bounds are satisfied).
Logical Words and, or, not, mod Boolean connectives and modulo arithmetic; Unicode ∧, ∨, ¬ are also supported.

Special Operators & Mathematical Unicode

≔ / := Directed Assignment Assigns an evaluated expression to a slot or target variable.
[] Root Node The Conway tree root node 0 born on Day 0 with empty path "".
++ Tree Branch / Concat Extends a tree sign sequence by appending a + or - child branch.
⊕, ⊖ Dyadic Add / Sub Direct bit-level addition/subtraction on aligned 2-successor trees.
⊗, ⊘ Dyadic Mul / Div Direct bit-level multiplication/division on aligned 2-successor trees.

X[a .. b] Prefix Slice Extracts the proper ancestral prefix of node X from birthday a to b.
≤, ≥, ≠ Relational Order Lexicographical tree ordering comparing birthday depth and branch signs.

🔄 The Interpreter Boundary Adapter

When the PseudoInterpreter is invoked by the Equation Evaluator or CRUD Workbench, it performs automatic boundary adaptation:

  1. Input Casting: Numbers passed from slider inputs (e.g. 1.5) are automatically mapped to their exact dyadic tree representation (e.g. node([+ + -])).
  2. Standard Part Extraction: If the target codomain is ℝ or 𝔻, the interpreter applies the Middle Way st(·) projection, dropping any residual halo dust O(dx).
  3. Boolean Normalization: Predicate rules returning numeric flags are converted to crisp Booleans {true, false} ∈ 𝔹.

🧰 4. Standard Built-in Primitive Functions

The MWM interpreter provides an ambient standard library directly callable within any pseudocode block:

Tree Topology & Conway Simplicity

  • EmptySet(): Allocates a new, empty set of tree nodes.
  • Insert(set, node): Inserts a tree node into the set in-place.
  • Maximum(set) / Minimum(set): Returns the greatest / least tree node under Conway lexicographical order.
  • length(X) / birthday(X): Returns the tree depth (birthday) of node X.
  • SimplerOptions(X): Returns the pair (XL, XR) of all ancestral prefixes born on earlier days.
  • Cut(leftBound, rightBound): Walks from root [] to find the unique simplest node strictly between bounds.

Dyadic Arithmetic & Bit Mechanics

  • DyadicAdd(x, y): Exact dyadic rational addition on binary tree structures.
  • sqr(x): Exact dyadic squaring (x ⊗ x).
  • to_dyadic(n) / node(path): Converts between sign strings and dyadic tree nodes.

Continuous & Nonstandard Analysis

  • st(x): Extracts the real standard part nucleus from a hyperreal dual number.
  • eps(x): Extracts the infinitesimal halo dust magnitude (multiples of dx ≔ 1/ω).
  • near(a, b, [tol]): Tests nonstandard infinitesimal proximity (a ≈ b).

Physical Dynamics, Rotation & Bayesian Inference

  • KinematicStep(s, v, dt): Symplectic leapfrog update returning [v_new, s_new] with zero energy drift.
  • CordicRotor(theta, iterations): Computes exact trigonometric coordinates [cos, sin] via dyadic shift-and-add operations.
  • BayesUpdate(priorH, pE_H, pE_notH): Computes exact normalized posterior probability on the hyperfinite unit transect.

⏱️ 5. The Interactive Stepper Engine & Telemetry

Unlike a standard "black box" code runner, the MWM PseudoInterpreter is compiled as an ES6 Generator (runStepper(entryFunctionName, args)). Each statement execution yields a snapshot containing: 

export interface IStepState {
  currentLine: number;                // Source line currently executing
  callStack: string[];                // Nested call stack frames (e.g. ConwayAdd -> Cut)
  variables: Record<string, any>;     // Snapshot of all active local variables
  isDone: boolean;                    // Has the algorithm completed?
  result?: any;                       // Return value if finished
  error?: string;                     // Exception or stack trace if faulted
  telemetry: IExecutionTelemetry;     // Physical resource counters
}
📊 The Ambient System Resource Ledger

To teach algorithmic complexity constructively, the interpreter maintains a hardware ledger:

  • stepCount: Total atomic operations executed on the discrete tree.
  • cutCount: Total Conway simplicity cuts invoked (measuring mediant walk costs).
  • maxCallDepth: Maximum recursive stack depth (measuring spatial memory requirements).
  • addCount / mulCount: Arithmetic operations in the underlying dyadic ring.

🏛️ 6. The Canonized MWM Pseudocode Rules

Here are three foundational rules illustrating how the Directed Equation signature maps directly to the operational code:

Rule 1: Conway Cut (Earliest Birthday Node Between Bounds)

Directed Equation Signature: (leftBound: Node, rightBound: Node) ⟹ candidate: Node
Lean 4 Theorem: MiddleWay.D_w_dense_in_R_w 
rule Cut(leftBound: Node, rightBound: Node) : Node ≔
var
    candidate: Node;
begin
    // Walk down the binary tree from the root []
    candidate := [];
    while (candidate <= leftBound) or (candidate >= rightBound) do
    begin
        if candidate <= leftBound then
            candidate := candidate ++ '+'      // Branch right to grow
        else
            candidate := candidate ++ '-';     // Branch left to shrink
    end;
    return candidate;  // Unique simplest node strictly between bounds
end;

Rule 2: Simpler Ancestor Options

Directed Equation Signature: (X: Node) ⟹ (XL: Set of Node, XR: Set of Node)
Lean 4 Theorem: MiddleWay.Tree1_is_well_ordered 
rule SimplerOptions(X: Node) : (Set of Node, Set of Node) ≔
var
    XL, XR: Set of Node;
    i: Integer;
    prefix: Node;
begin
    XL := EmptySet();
    XR := EmptySet();

    // All proper prefixes are numbers born on earlier days
    for i := 0 to length(X) - 1 do
    begin
        prefix := X[0 .. i];
        if prefix < X then
            Insert(XL, prefix)
        else
            Insert(XR, prefix);
    end;

    return (XL, XR);
end;

Rule 3: Kinematic Velocity Decrement on ℝ_ω

Directed Equation Signature: (v₀: ℝ_ω, g: ℝ_ω, t: ℝ_ω) ⟹ v: ℝ_ω
Lean 4 Theorem: MiddleWay.free_fall_stencil 
rule FreeFallVelocity(v0: ℝ_ω, g: ℝ_ω, t: ℝ_ω) : ℝ_ω ≔
var
    v: ℝ_ω;
begin
    // Symplectic linear velocity update
    v := v0 - (g * t);
    return v;
end;
